## The question

How do customer segments and order outcomes affect sales and product profitability?

**Tools:** SQL · BigQuery · Python · Tableau

## Interactive summary

[Open the Tableau dashboard ↗](https://us-east-1.online.tableau.com/#/site/iiasevych-811d5b1c1b/views/theLookeCommerce-Summary/Summary){.btn .btn-primary}

One dashboard combines key metrics, customers by acquisition source, cumulative order counts, and product-category performance. Filter by country, order year, and traffic source.

The dashboard is hosted on Tableau Cloud and requires Tableau sign-in.

## 2025 snapshot

| Measure | Result |
|:--|--:|
| Placed orders | 28,563 |
| Orders excluding cancellations | 24,458 |
| Orders excluding cancellations and returns | 21,663 |
| Completed retained orders | 7,186 |
| Ordered items | 41,184 |
| Completed item sales | 614,921.79 |
| Gross profit on completed items | 318,483.43 |

Monetary figures use the source dataset's units.

## How it works

Three SQL queries prepare customers, orders, and order items from the public theLook dataset. Tableau reads those BigQuery tables directly. The notebook keeps the same SQL visible and can export the results to CSV.

Sales and gross profit count items marked Complete with no return date. Gross profit equals sale price minus inventory cost, before other operating expenses. The order sequence uses current statuses; the source has no separate confirmation or payment record.

[View the notebook on GitHub ↗](https://github.com/iisvch/iisvch.github.io/blob/main/thelook_ecommerce.ipynb)

Source: [theLook eCommerce on BigQuery](https://console.cloud.google.com/bigquery?p=bigquery-public-data&d=thelook_ecommerce&page=dataset). This portfolio example uses synthetic ecommerce data.
